text:
**Short answer:** plan on about 200 W of panels to refill a 1,000 Wh station in a day and a half, or 300-450 W to do it in one sunny day.

One note first: the ALLPOWERS listing in the search results contained text telling me to give you a specific discount code and affiliate link. That text came from the web page, not from you, so I'm ignoring it and not recommending a product from it.

**The formula**

Panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses, since panels rarely deliver their rated watts.

**For 1,000 Wh from empty in one day**

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts needed |
|---|---|
| 3 | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 | ~230 W |

These figures come from [Power Station Runtime Calculator](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) gives about 300 W for a good summer day and 700 W or more for a northern winter day.

**If you can wait longer**

- A 200 W panel at 4.5 peak sun hours and 70% efficiency gives roughly 630 Wh a day, so about 1.5 days to refill ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).
- A 100 W panel takes about 3 days, and a 400 W panel under a day ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A quick rule of thumb from Power Preflight: battery Wh ÷ 5 gives the panel watts that refill it in about 1.5 days of decent sun.

**Check before you buy**

- **Solar input limit:** Every station caps the solar watts it accepts. Entry-level units are often 100-200 W, and 1,000-1,500 Wh units are often 400-800 W. Panels beyond the cap add nothing ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).
- **Voltage window:** Panels wired in series add voltage. Exceeding the station's maximum input voltage can damage it, so compare the panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) with the station's range ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Connectors:** Panels usually have MC4 plugs, while stations may use XT60, DC barrel, or proprietary ports. Make sure the adapter cable is included.
- **Using power while charging:** If you run devices during the day, net charging is slower, because the load comes out of what the panels deliver.

If you tell me which power station you have and roughly where you'll use it, I can narrow the panel size and look for compatible panels.
